```{r}
logitsToProbabilities <- function(x){
    if(any(is.na(x))){
        stop('ERROR - There are NAs in your supplied x. Remove them first.')
    }
    out <- exp(x)/(1 + exp(x))
    return(out)
}

calculate_auprc <- function(dt, ycolumn = 'AR_Prostate', labelcolumn = "binding_class", ...){
    dt <- dt[complete.cases(dt), ]
    tryCatch({
        pr <- PRROC::pr.curve(scores.class0 = dt[[ycolumn]], weights.class0=dt[[labelcolumn]], curve = FALSE)
        return(pr$auc.integral)
    }, error = function(e){
        return(NA)
    })
}

calculate_auroc <- function(dt, ycolumn = 'AR_Prostate', labelcolumn = "binding_class"){
    dt <- dt[complete.cases(dt), ]
    pp <- pROC::roc(dt[[labelcolumn]], dt[[ycolumn]], quiet = TRUE)
    pp_auc <- pp$auc |> as.numeric()
    return(pp_auc)
}
# ci.auc(test_need$beat_budget, test_pred) 
calculate_ci_auroc <- function(dt, ycolumn = 'AR_Prostate', labelcolumn = "binding_class"){
    dt <- dt[complete.cases(dt), ]
    pp <- pROC::ci.auc(response = dt[[labelcolumn]], predictor = dt[[ycolumn]], quiet = TRUE)
    pp_ci <- pp$conf.level #|> as.numeric()
    return(pp_ci)
}

# https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73611070/sample-percentages-in-different-groups-without-repeating-r

create_varying_proportions <- function(dt, prop_neg, prop_pos, total_num = 4000){
    pos_xt <- base::subset(dt, binding_class == 1)
    neg_xt <- base::subset(dt, binding_class == 0)
    neg <- neg_xt %>% 
        slice_sample(n = ceiling(total_num * prop_neg))
    pos <- pos_xt %>% 
        slice_sample(n = ceiling(total_num * prop_pos))

    dt_varying_proportions <- dplyr::bind_rows(neg, pos)
    return(dt_varying_proportions)
}



resample_data <- function(labels, predictions, measure = c('roc', 'pr')){
    indices.sample <- sample(1:length(labels), size = length(labels), replace = TRUE)
    labels.sample <- labels[indices.sample]
    predictions.sample <- predictions[indices.sample]
    if(measure == 'roc'){
        pp <- pROC::roc(labels.sample, predictions.sample, quiet = TRUE)
        vv <- pp$auc |> as.numeric()
    } else if (measure == 'pr'){
        pp <- PRROC::pr.curve(scores.class0 = predictions.sample, weights.class0=labels.sample, curve = FALSE)
        vv <- pp$auc.integral
    }
    
    return(vv)
}

calculate_confidence_intervals <- function(dt, ycolumn, labelcolumn, measure, nreplicates = 1000){
    dt <- dt[complete.cases(dt), ]
    auc.vv.samples <- replicate(1000, resample_data(dt[[labelcolumn]], dt[[ycolumn]], measure = measure), simplify=TRUE)
    lower_bound <- quantile(auc.vv.samples, 0.025)
    upper_bound <- quantile(auc.vv.samples, 0.975)
    mean_value <- mean(auc.vv.samples)
    median_value <- median(auc.vv.samples)
    return(c(lower_bound, mean = mean_value, median = median_value, upper_bound))
}

qqcompare.ggplot <- function(p1, p2, names = c('observed', 'null'), mlog10_p_thres=30){
    require(ggplot2)
    ## thresholded by default at 1e-30
    p1 = na.omit(p1)
    p2 = na.omit(p2)
    p_thres = 10^{-mlog10_p_thres}
    if(!is.null(p_thres)){pvec1 = pmax(p1, p_thres); pvec2 = pmax(p2, p_thres)}
    nn = length(pvec1)
    xx =  -log10((1:nn)/(nn+1))

    pp <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
        geom_point(aes(x = xx, y = -sort(log10(pvec1)), col = names[1])) +
        geom_point(aes(x = xx, y = -sort(log10(pvec2)), col = names[2])) +
        labs(x = expression(Expected~~-log[10](italic(p))),
          y = expression(Observed~~-log[10](italic(p)))) +
          geom_abline(aes(intercept = 0, slope = 1), col='gray', lty = 1)
        
    return(pp)
}

qqunif.ggplot <- function(p, mlog10_p_thres=30){
    require(ggplot2)
    ## thresholded by default at 1e-30
    p=na.omit(p)
    nn = length(p)
    xx =  -log10((1:nn)/(nn+1))
    
    p_thres = 10^{-mlog10_p_thres}
    if(sum(p < p_thres)){
      warning(paste("thresholding p to ", p_thres))
      p = pmax(p, p_thres)
    }

    dt <- data.table(pval = xx, dist = -sort(log10(p)))

    pp <- ggplot2::ggplot(dt, aes(x = pval, y = dist)) +
        geom_point() +
        labs(x = expression(Expected~~-log[10](italic(p))),
          y = expression(Observed~~-log[10](italic(p)))) +
          geom_abline(aes(intercept = 0, slope = 1), col='gray', lty = 1)
        
    return(pp)
}
```

```{r}
theme_simple <- theme_bw() + theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(family = 'Helvetica', colour = 'black', size = 9.33),
    text=element_text(size=9.33, colour = 'black', family = 'Helvetica'),
    axis.text = element_text(hjust = 1), 
    axis.text.x = element_text( hjust=0.5), 
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill=NA, linewidth=0.5)
)

plot_pr_curve.ggplot <- function(pr_object, tf_tissue){
    dt_pr_curve <- pr_object$curve %>% as.data.table() %>% setnames(c('recall', 'precision', 'unk'))

    tlabel <- glue("AUPRC: {round(pr_object$auc.integral, 3)}")
    ttitle <- glue("Precision-Recall curve for\nEnpact's {tf_tissue} Model")

    pp <- dt_pr_curve %>% ggplot(aes(x = recall, y = precision)) +
        ggplot2::geom_line() +
        ylim(0, 1) +
        xlim(0, 1) +
        labs(x = 'Recall', y = 'Precision', title = ttitle) +
        theme_simple +
        geom_text(label = tlabel, col = 'darkgreen', x = 0.2, y = 0.2, size = 2.0)

    return(pp)

    #
}
```

# Comment 1
```{verbatim}
The model leverages variation across the genome rather than variation across individuals. 
However, this implicitly assumes that identical sequences have identical regulatory effects regardless of genomic context. 
The authors should justify their assumption and elaborate better on the validity of this choice.
```

# Comment 2
```{verbatim}
The reported AUROC values appear very high, raising concerns that 
the test did not have a balanced number of positives and negatives 
(considering that positives are much rarer than negatives). 
In this regard, reporting the area under the precision-recall curve 
(AUPRC) may be a more informative metric.
```

## Reviewer 2's comment 1: Performance (test AUROC vs train truly bound sites)
```{verbatim}
It may be helpful to assess whether model performance correlates with the number of unique ChIP-seq peaks used for training. While performance is evaluated relative to the number of ChIP-seq experiments, this does not necessarily reflect the diversity of binding events contributing to each model. Examining performance as a function of unique bound sites could clarify how much effective training signal supports each TF-tissue pair and help contextualize confidence in downstream associations.
```


## Show AUPRC for one from each decile

```{r}
# group by deciles and select one each
set.seed(2024)
dt_deciles <- dt %>% dplyr::filter(type == 'test') %>% dplyr::select(assay, context, model, auprc) %>% 
    mutate(decile_rank = ntile(auprc, 10)) %>%
    group_by(decile_rank) 
    
topsamples <- dt_deciles %>%
    slice_max(n = 1)

if(!"AR_Prostate" %in% topsamples$model){
    addt <- dt_deciles %>% dplyr::filter(model == 'AR_Prostate')
    topsamples <- bind_rows(topsamples, addt)
}

topsamples
```

```{r}
eval_files <- Sys.glob(glue("{tfxcan_project_directory}/data/enpact/evaluations/{topsamples$assay}_{topsamples$context}_*.logistic.test_eval.txt.gz"))

auprc_deciles <- purrr::map(seq_along(eval_files), function(i){
    dt <- data.table::fread(eval_files[i])
    dt <- dt[complete.cases(dt), ]
    dtx <- topsamples[i, ]
    pr <- PRROC::pr.curve(scores.class0 = dt[['TFPred_score']], weights.class0=dt[['binding_class']], curve = TRUE)
    prplot <- plot_pr_curve.ggplot(pr, glue("{dtx$assay}-{dtx$context}"))
    return(prplot)
        
})
```

```{r,fig.width = 24, fig.height = 8}
pp <- patchwork::wrap_plots(rev(auprc_deciles), ncol = 6)
ggsave(glue("{figures_directory}/SF1.AUPRC.test.deciles.png"), pp, width = 12000, height = 4000, dpi = 800, units = 'px')
pp
```

```{r}
plot_pr_curve.ggplot <- function(pr_object, tf_tissue){
    dt_pr_curve <- pr_object$curve %>% as.data.table() %>% setnames(c('recall', 'precision', 'unk'))

    tlabel <- glue("AUPRC: {round(pr_object$auc.integral, 3)}")
    ttitle <- glue("Precision-Recall curve for\nEnpact's {tf_tissue} Model")

    pp <- dt_pr_curve %>% ggplot(aes(x = recall, y = precision)) +
        ggplot2::geom_line() +
        ylim(0, 1) +
        xlim(0, 1) +
        labs(x = 'Recall', y = 'Precision', title = ttitle) +
        theme_simple +
        geom_text(label = tlabel, col = 'darkgreen', x = 0.8, y = 0.9, size = 2.0)

    #ggsave(file.path(figures_directory, "AUPRC.AR_Prostate.png"), pp, width = 2000, height = 2000, dpi = 800, units = 'px')
}
```

```{r}
proportion_of_negatives <- seq(0.1, 0.9, 0.05)
proportion_of_positives <- 1 - proportion_of_negatives
varying_prauc <- sapply(seq_along(proportion_of_negatives), function(i){
    xt <- create_varying_proportions(dt_predictions, prop_neg = proportion_of_negatives[i], prop_pos = proportion_of_positives[i], total_num = 4000)
    prauc.value <- pr.curve(scores.class0 = xt$AR_Prostate, weights.class0 = xt$binding_class)$auc.integral
    return(prauc.value)
})

varying_auprc <- data.table(prop_neg = proportion_of_negatives, prop_pos = proportion_of_positives, auprc = varying_prauc)
varying_auprc |> head()
```

# Comment 3 and 4 (similar ideas)
```{verbatim}
This very high performance might be caused by data leakage. 
It is therefore crucial to validate that the models were not trained on correlated datasets. 
Specifically, the authors show that TF ChIP-seq is the most informative feature. This makes it necessary to exclude any features derived from tissues that 
overlap with the test tissue and check performance when Enformer 
does not include the target TF 
(or highly correlated ones) in its training data. For example, what would happen if all FOXA1-related features are removed (e.g. the lung ChIP-seq data of FOXA1)? 

1) If performance remains unchanged, this would strengthen the claim that the model learned generalizable regulatory logic. 

2) If it drops modestly, then FOXa1 is likely mildly correlated with AR binding, which could still support generalizability but with some caveats.

3) If it drops significantly, then this raises concerns about leakage of training data, even if AR itself was never directly observed by Enformer… 
```

```{verbatim}
More generally, could the authors remove all Enformer features corresponding to TF binding (another source of possible circularity) and retrain it to see how the performance drops?
```

## 4. Calculate metrics for all three features predictors analysis
```{r}
feature_sets <- c('no_prostate_features', 'no_prostate_foxa1_features', 'no_tf_features')

feature_sets.full_names <- c("No prostate features", "No prostate or FOXA1 features", "No transcription factor-related features")
names(feature_sets.full_names) <- feature_sets

feature_sets.predicted_binding <- purrr::map(feature_sets, function(feau){
    xt <- data.table::fread(glue::glue('{tfxcan_directory}/experiments/auprc/AR_Prostate.{feau}.predictions.txt.gz'))
    if("AR_Prostate_weights" %in% colnames(xt)){
        xt <- xt %>% dplyr::rename(AR_Prostate = AR_Prostate_weights)
    }

    return(xt)
})

names(feature_sets.predicted_binding) <- feature_sets

# calculate perfromance metrics
set.seed(2025)
feature_sets.performance <- purrr::map(feature_sets, function(feau){
    auroc.ci <- calculate_confidence_intervals(feature_sets.predicted_binding[[feau]], 'AR_Prostate', 'binding_class', measure = 'roc', nreplicates = 5000)
    auprc.ci <- calculate_confidence_intervals(feature_sets.predicted_binding[[feau]], 'AR_Prostate', 'binding_class', measure = 'pr', nreplicates = 5000)
    data.frame(
        auprc = calculate_auprc(feature_sets.predicted_binding[[feau]], ycolumn = 'AR_Prostate', labelcolumn = 'binding_class'), 
        auroc = calculate_auroc(feature_sets.predicted_binding[[feau]], ycolumn = 'AR_Prostate', labelcolumn = 'binding_class'), 
        auprc.lower = auprc.ci['2.5%'],
        auprc.upper = auprc.ci['97.5%'],
        auroc.lower = auroc.ci['2.5%'],
        auroc.upper = auroc.ci['97.5%'],
        row.names = feature_sets.full_names[feau]) %>% round(3)
        
}) %>% do.call('rbind', .) %>% as.data.table(keep.rownames ='feature')

feature_sets.performance
```

Further, training (as well as hyperparameter tuning and feature selection) was done on the training set only. 
See training code below [here](https://github.com/hakyimlab/TFPred-snakemake/blob/main/workflow/src/train_enet.R)

- X_train: A matrix of motif sites designated to be trained on
- binding_class: a vector of 0 and 1's of binding status
- nfolds: number of cross-validation folds on the input `X_train` training data

```{r, eval = F}
#| code-fold: false
cv_model <- tryCatch({
        glmnet::cv.glmnet(x=X_train, y=binding_class, family = "binomial", type.measure = "auc", alpha = 0.5, keep=T, parallel=T, nfolds=opt$nfolds, trace.it=F)
    }, error = function(e){
        print(glue('ERROR - {e}'))
        return(NULL)
})

```

Evaluation was done on training and test data separately. See the source code [here](https://github.com/hakyimlab/TFPred-snakemake/blob/main/workflow/src/evaluate_enet.R)

```{r, eval = F}
#| code-fold: false
for(i in seq_along(models)){
    # read in the newx data : train or test
    newx_list <- purrr::map(.x=c(opt$train_data_file, opt$test_data_file), function(each_data){
        mat_dt <- data.table::fread(each_data)
        newx <- as.matrix(mat_dt[, -c(1:3)])
        # you only need one : link
        link_pred <- predict(models[[i]], newx, s = "lambda.1se", type = 'link') |> as.vector()
        response_pred <- predict(models[[i]], newx, s = "lambda.1se", type = 'response') |> as.vector()
        df <- mat_dt[, c(1:3)] |> as.data.frame()
        df$TFPred_score <- link_pred
        df$probability <- response_pred
        colnames(df) <- c('locus', 'binding_class', 'binding_counts', 'TFPred_score', 'probability')
        return(df)
    }, .progress=T)
}
```

# Comment 6

```{verbatim}
Also, since the goal is to predict TF binding regardless of motif presence, 
would it not be more valuable to evaluate on true genome-wide negatives rather 
than motif-matched decoys. For example, the authors should select all 
random 600 bp genomics windows genome-wide, label windows overlapping 
ChIP peaks as positive and use all other windows, again, 
regardless of motif presence, as negative. This would allow predicting 
where TFs bind in the entire genome, not just to strong motif-containing sites.
```

In this section, I will test

1. Chip+motif-based predictors on chip+motif-based test set (Already done, in the paper)

2. Chip+motif-based predictors on chip-based test set

3. Chip-based predictors on chip+motif-based test set

4. Chip-based predictors on chip-based test set


## Train on chip-based curated regions (as opposed to chip+motif-based regions) and test on (1) the curated test set above, and (2) test on the chip-based curated regions, too. And on GWAS loci.


These are all AR Prostate peaks across the genome. Will be needed later. 

### Step 1. Select some 100000 random windows across the genome. 
    (To make sure I have enough to train and test on, I will select some 100000 intervals)
```{bash, eval = F}

# genome file : /beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFPred-snakemake/info/hg38.chrom.sizes.sorted
bedtools random -l 512 -n 100000 -g /beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFPred-snakemake/info/hg38.chrom.sizes.sorted -seed 1865 > /beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFXcan/experiments/random_windows/random_100000windows.bed
```

### Step 2. Divide into bound and unbound.

```{r}
library(rtracklayer)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(plyranges)

valid_chromosomes <- paste0('chr', 1:22)
```

```{r}
# gr_obj <- rtracklayer::import("/beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFXcan/experiments/random_windows/random_100000windows.bed")
# rtracklayer::import("/beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFXcan/experiments/random_windows/random_100000windows.bed")
random_sites.granges <- rtracklayer::import("/beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFXcan/experiments/random_windows/random_100000windows.bed")

# cistrome AR Prostate peaks (will be used to define bound and unbound)
# read in, turn to granges and reduce
# reducing will help prevent double counting
cistrome_AR_peaks.granges <- data.table::fread(file.path(tfxcan_directory, 'experiments/gwas/cistrome_peaks.AR_Prostate.sorted.bed'), col.names = c('chrom', 'start', 'end', 'id_num', 'width', 'strand', 'score', 'neglog10p', 'neglog10q', 'value')) %>% 
    with(GenomicRanges::GRanges(seqnames = chrom, ranges = IRanges(start, end), strand = '*')) %>% GenomicRanges::reduce()

cistrome_AR_peaks.granges <- GenomeInfoDb::keepSeqlevels(cistrome_AR_peaks.granges, valid_chromosomes, pruning.mode = "coarse")
```

- Remove random sites overlapping the test motifs (i.e. just remove chrom 9 and 22)

```{r}
#training_data.granges <- random_sites.granges[!seqnames(random_sites.granges) %in% c('chr9', 'chr22')]

# remember to ignore the strand information
ovlaps <- findOverlaps(query = random_sites.granges, subject = cistrome_AR_peaks.granges, ignore.strand = TRUE)

# bound
bound <- random_sites.granges[queryHits(ovlaps)]
unbound <- random_sites.granges[-queryHits(ovlaps)]

mcols(bound)$status <- 1
mcols(unbound)$status <- 0

training_data.granges <- unique(c(bound, unbound))

training_data.dt <- training_data.granges %>% plyranges::mutate(
    chrom = as.character(seqnames)
  ) %>% plyranges::mutate(set =
    case_when(
      !chrom %in% c('chr9', 'chr22') ~ "train",
      chrom %in% c('chr9', 'chr22') ~ "test" # Default case
    )) %>% as.data.table() %>% dplyr::select(-seqnames) %>% dplyr::relocate(chrom)

training_data.dt <- training_data.dt %>% dplyr::filter(chrom %in% valid_chromosomes)
```

```{r}
predictions <- purrr::map(X_test.list, function(X_test){
    X <- X_test %>% dplyr::select(starts_with("f_")) |> as.matrix()
    y <- X_test %>% dplyr::select(!starts_with("f_")) |> as.data.frame()
    rownames(X) <- y$locus
    Xpred <- as.matrix(X %*% wgts[-1,,drop = FALSE]) + wgts[1,]
    Xpred <- Xpred %>% as.data.table(keep.rownames = 'locus') %>% dplyr::inner_join(y, by = 'locus')
    Xpred
})

metrics.auprc <- purrr::map(names(predictions), function(nt){
    random_windows <- calculate_auprc(predictions[[nt]], ycolumn = 'random_windows_wgts', labelcolumn = "binding_class") %>% round(2)
    motifs <- calculate_auprc(predictions[[nt]], ycolumn = 'motifs_wgts', labelcolumn = "binding_class") %>% round(2)


    data.table(method = nt, random_windows, motifs)
}) %>% dplyr::bind_rows() 

metrics.auroc <- purrr::map(names(predictions), function(nt){
    random_windows <- calculate_auroc(predictions[[nt]], ycolumn = 'random_windows_wgts', labelcolumn = "binding_class") %>% round(2)
    motifs <- calculate_auroc(predictions[[nt]], ycolumn = 'motifs_wgts', labelcolumn = "binding_class") %>% round(2)
    data.table(method = nt, random_windows, motifs)
}) %>% dplyr::bind_rows() 


ci.auprc <- purrr::map(names(predictions), function(nt){
    ci.random_windows <- calculate_confidence_intervals(predictions[[nt]], 'random_windows_wgts', 'binding_class', measure = 'pr', nreplicates = 5000) %>% round(2)
    ci.motifs <- calculate_confidence_intervals(predictions[[nt]], 'motifs_wgts', 'binding_class', measure = 'pr', nreplicates = 5000) %>% round(2)

    data.table(method = nt, 
        random_windows.lower = ci.random_windows['2.5%'], 
        random_windows.upper = ci.random_windows['97.5%'], 
        motifs.lower = ci.motifs['2.5%'], 
        motifs.upper = ci.motifs['97.5%'])
}) %>% dplyr::bind_rows()

ci.auroc <- purrr::map(names(predictions), function(nt){
    ci.random_windows <- calculate_confidence_intervals(predictions[[nt]], 'random_windows_wgts', 'binding_class', measure = 'roc', nreplicates = 5000) %>% round(2)
    ci.motifs <- calculate_confidence_intervals(predictions[[nt]], 'motifs_wgts', 'binding_class', measure = 'roc', nreplicates = 5000) %>% round(2)

    data.table(method = nt, 
        random_windows.lower = ci.random_windows['2.5%'], 
        random_windows.upper = ci.random_windows['97.5%'], 
        motifs.lower = ci.motifs['2.5%'], 
        motifs.upper = ci.motifs['97.5%'])
}) %>% dplyr::bind_rows()


metrics.auprc <- data.table::transpose(metrics.auprc, keep.names = "method", make.names = 1)
metrics.auroc <- data.table::transpose(metrics.auroc, keep.names = "method", make.names = 1)


metrics.auprc; metrics.auroc
```

```{r}
data.table::transpose(ci.auroc, keep.names = "method", make.names = 1)
```

```{r, eval = F}
gwas_assoc.bound_unbound <- gwas_assoc.granges %>%
    purrr::map(function(each_grange){
        ov_granges <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(query = each_grange, subject = granges_ar_peaks_windows)
        bound <- each_grange[queryHits(ov_granges)]
        unbound <- each_grange[-queryHits(ov_granges)]

        mcols(bound)$status <- 'bound'
        mcols(unbound)$status <- 'unbound'

        return(c(bound, unbound))
    })

set.seed(2025)
```

## Compare Enpact’s AR predicted binding to predicted ATAC seq peaks (you will need to train a model here)

For this comment, I collect genome-wide ATAC peaks for AR in prostate tissues. 
I filter out those in the training and test sets based on binding or no binding. 

I also collected closed chromatin regions (and annotated binding or no binding). 

Then I divided the rest into those with an AR peak and those without, and predicted binding using the AR-Prostate model.

Notes:

    - Difference between findOverlaps and subsetByOverlaps: https://www.biostars.org/p/473162/

```{r}
atac_cistrome <- data.table::fread("/project2/haky/Data/TFXcan/cistrome/raw/human_ca_full_QC.txt") %>%
    dplyr::filter(Tissue_type == 'Prostate') # Factor == 'ATAC-seq' 

valid_chromosomes <- paste0('chr', 1:22)
atac_cistrome.prostate <- glue::glue("/project2/haky/Data/TFXcan/cistrome/raw/human_ca/{atac_cistrome$DCid}_sort_peaks.narrowPeak.bed") %>%
    purrr::map(function(ff){
        tryCatch({
            xt <- data.table::fread(ff) %>%
                dplyr::select(chr=V1, start=V2, end=V3, strand = V6) %>% 
                dplyr::filter(chr %in% valid_chromosomes)
            if(nrow(xt) > 0){
                xt <- with(xt, GRanges(chr, IRanges(start, end), strand="*")) %>% GenomicRanges::reduce()
                return(xt)
            } else {
                return(NULL)
            }
        }, error = function(err){
            return(err)
        })
    })

atac_cistrome.prostate <- Filter(Negate(is.null), atac_cistrome.prostate)
atac_cistrome.prostate <- atac_cistrome.prostate %>% as(., "GRangesList") %>% unlist(., recursive = TRUE, use.names = TRUE)
background.AR_prostate <- atac_cistrome.prostate[seqnames(atac_cistrome.prostate) %in% valid_chromosomes]
seqlevels(background.AR_prostate) <- valid_chromosomes
background.AR_prostate <- sort(background.AR_prostate) %>% GenomicRanges::reduce()
background.AR_prostate |> head()

background.AR_prostate %>% 
    as.data.table() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(peak = glue("peak{1:nrow(.)}")) %>%
    data.table::fwrite(file.path(tfxcan_directory, 'experiments/atac/background.atac_peaks.AR_Prostate.windows.bed'), sep = '\t', quote = F, col.names = F, row.names = F)
```

```{r}
accessibility_peaks.AR_Prostate <- data.table::fread(file.path(tfxcan_directory, 'experiments/atac/background.atac_peaks.AR_Prostate.windows.bed')) %>%
    with(GRanges(V1, IRanges(V2, V3), strand="*")) %>% GenomicRanges::reduce()
```

### Create bound vs unbound based on TF presence.
```{r}
# genomewide AR peaks in prostate tissues
# reducing will help prevent double counting
chip.AR_prostate <- data.table::fread('/beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFXcan/experiments/random_windows/cistrome_peaks.AR.sorted.bed', col.names = c('chrom', 'start', 'end', 'id_num', 'width', 'strand', 'score', 'neglog10p', 'neglog10q', 'value')) %>% with(GenomicRanges::GRanges(seqnames = chrom, ranges = IRanges(start, end), strand = '*')) %>% GenomicRanges::reduce()
valid_chromosomes <- paste0('chr', 1:22)
chip.AR_prostate <- GenomeInfoDb::keepSeqlevels(chip.AR_prostate, valid_chromosomes, pruning.mode = "coarse")
chip.AR_prostate |> head()
```

```{r}
# take overlaps
ovlaps <- findOverlaps(query = accessibility_peaks.AR_Prostate, subject = chip.AR_prostate)
atac_bound.AR_Prostate <- accessibility_peaks.AR_Prostate[queryHits(ovlaps)] %>% reduce()
atac_unbound.AR_Prostate <- accessibility_peaks.AR_Prostate[-queryHits(ovlaps)] %>% reduce()
```

Should I select peaks > say 512bp
or 

```{r}
# select only those whose distance to the nearest is greater than 512kb (because of enformer), here 10kb
dnear <- GenomicRanges::distanceToNearest(x = atac_bound.AR_Prostate, subject = atac_unbound.AR_Prostate)
dnear <- dnear[mcols(dnear)$distance > 10000]
sum(mcols(dnear)$distance > 10000)

atac_bound.AR_Prostate <- atac_bound.AR_Prostate[queryHits(dnear)] %>% reduce()
atac_unbound.AR_Prostate <- atac_unbound.AR_Prostate[unique(subjectHits(dnear))] %>% reduce()
```

```{r}
# check the distances again
newdnear <- GenomicRanges::distanceToNearest(x = atac_bound.AR_Prostate, subject = atac_unbound.AR_Prostate)
all(mcols(newdnear)$distance > 10000)

# join
mcols(atac_bound.AR_Prostate)$status <- 1
mcols(atac_unbound.AR_Prostate)$status <- 0
training_data.granges <- c(atac_bound.AR_Prostate, atac_unbound.AR_Prostate) %>%
    resize(fix = 'center', width = 512)

mcols(training_data.granges)$id <- paste0('peak_', 1:length(training_data.granges))
```

```{r}
# takes a while but it tells you what has been reduced or unionized, and I want to remove those largely because I am not sure if they are bound or unbound
grr <- reduce(training_data.granges, with.revmap = TRUE)

# add meta columns with collapse
mcols(grr) <- do.call(rbind,
                      lapply(mcols(grr)$revmap, function(i) {
                        data.frame(
                          name = paste(mcols(training_data.granges)$id[ i ], collapse = ","))
                        }))

grr_ids.split <- mcols(grr)$name %>% strsplit(',')
grr_ids.length <- sapply(grr_ids.split, length)
overlapping_peaks <- grr_ids.split[grr_ids.length > 1] %>% unlist()
training_data.granges.final <- training_data.granges %>% plyranges::filter(!id %in% overlapping_peaks)
```

```{r}
length(training_data.granges.final); width(training_data.granges.final) |> summary()
```

### Remove overlaps with the AR_Prostate binding test set



```{r}
### Does training include the test?
pred_binding.AR_Prostate <- data.table::fread(file.path(tfxcan_directory, "data/enpact/evaluations/AR_Prostate_2025-04-24.logistic.test_eval.txt.gz")) %>% dplyr::select(locus, binding_class, binding_score = TFPred_score) %>% distinct()

pred_binding.AR_Prostate.granges <- pred_binding.AR_Prostate %>%
    tidyr::separate_wider_delim(col = locus, delim = '_', names = c('chrom', 'start', 'end'), cols_remove = F) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(c(start, end), as.numeric)) %>%
    with(., GRanges(chrom, IRanges(start, end), strand="*", locus, binding_class, binding_score))


ovlaps <- findOverlaps(query = pred_binding.AR_Prostate.granges, subject = training_data.granges.final)

# remove those from the training_data.granges.final
training_data.granges.final <- training_data.granges.final[-subjectHits(ovlaps)]
```


```{r}

# it is possible that there are still some overlaps with the bound or unbound

training_data.dt <- training_data.granges.final %>% plyranges::mutate(
    chrom = as.character(seqnames)
  ) %>% plyranges::mutate(set =
    case_when(
      !chrom %in% c('chr9', 'chr22') ~ "train",
      chrom %in% c('chr9', 'chr22') ~ "test" # Default case
    )) %>% as.data.table() %>% dplyr::select(-seqnames) %>% dplyr::relocate(chrom)

training_data.dt <- training_data.dt %>% dplyr::filter(chrom %in% valid_chromosomes)
```

#### Predict accessibility
```{r}
accessibility_wgts.AR_Prostate <- data.table::fread(glue("{tfxcan_directory}/experiments/atac/accessibility.AR_Prostate.weights.tsv.gz")) %>% tibble::column_to_rownames('feature') %>% as.matrix()

X_test.yhat <- accessibility_wgts.AR_Prostate[1,1] + as.matrix(X_test %*% accessibility_wgts.AR_Prostate[-1, , drop = FALSE])
```

This comment is similar to Reviewer 2 comment 2

```{verbatim}
It may be informative to explore an alternative classification task conditioned on accessibility. The current model is trained on all motif instances, regardless of chromatin state, which may conflate TF binding with general accessibility, since all sequences contain the motif and the primary difference between bound and unbound sites may simply reflect whether the site is accessible. 

As a complementary analysis, the authors could consider training models on motif instances restricted to accessible regions (e.g., experimental ATAC/DNase or predicted if not available), with labels indicating presence or absence of a TF ChIP-seq peak. Exploring this setup in a small subset of TF-tissue pairs may clarify whether different features are learned and provide more direct insight into TF binding preferences
```

### Split the test motif into ATAC or no ATAC peaks, and evaluate the peformance.

```{r}
motif_eval <- data.table::fread(file.path(tfxcan_directory, "data/enpact/evaluations/AR_Prostate_2025-04-24.logistic.test_eval.txt.gz")) %>% dplyr::select(locus, score = TFPred_score, binding_class) %>% dplyr::mutate(method = case_when(
    binding_class == 1 ~ "motif_bound",
    binding_class == 0 ~ 'motif_unbound'
)) %>% tidyr::separate_wider_delim(col = locus, delim = '_', names = c('chrom', 'start', 'end'), cols_remove = F) %>%
dplyr::mutate(across(c(start, end), as.numeric)) %>%
    with(., GRanges(chrom, IRanges(start, end), strand="*", locus, score, binding_class, method))
```

```{r}
# those in accessible regions
ovalaps <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(motif_eval, open.atac.background)
motif.accessible <- motif_eval[queryHits(ovalaps)] %>% as.data.table() %>% dplyr::mutate(feature = 'open')
# ovalaps <- findOverlaps(motif_eval, closed.atac.background)
motif.inaccessible <- motif_eval[-queryHits(ovalaps)] %>% as.data.table() %>% dplyr::mutate(feature = 'closed')
data_eval <- bind_rows(motif.accessible, motif.inaccessible) %>% dplyr::rename(status = method) 
```

```{r}
# split open and closed granges into bound and unbound based on chip seq

# select atac bound and unbound
atac_chip_overlap <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(query=open.atac.background, subject=chip.AR_prostate, type='any')
atac_bound <- open.atac.background[queryHits(atac_chip_overlap)]
atac_unbound <- open.atac.background[-queryHits(atac_chip_overlap)]

# select only those whose distance to the nearest is greater than 1000kb (because of enformer)
dnear <- GenomicRanges::distanceToNearest(x = atac_bound, subject = atac_unbound)
dnear <- dnear[mcols(dnear)$distance > 1000]

atac_bound <- atac_bound[queryHits(dnear)]
atac_unbound <- atac_unbound[subjectHits(dnear)]
```

```{r}
# do the same as above for the closed regions
non.atac_chip_overlap <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(query = closed.atac.background, subject=chip.AR_prostate, type='any')
non.atac_bound <- closed.atac.background[queryHits(non.atac_chip_overlap)]
non.atac_unbound <- closed.atac.background[-queryHits(non.atac_chip_overlap)]

# select only those whose distance to the nearest is greater than 1000kb (because of enformer)
dnear <- GenomicRanges::distanceToNearest(x = non.atac_bound, subject = non.atac_unbound)
dnear <- dnear[mcols(dnear)$distance > 1000]

non.atac_bound <- non.atac_bound[queryHits(dnear)]
non.atac_unbound <- non.atac_unbound[subjectHits(dnear)]
```

```{r}
# confirm there is not overlap by computing pairwise overlap between them
combbb <- combn(names(data_list), 2)

nnames <- c()
ovlaps_list <- apply(combbb, 2, function(each_dt){
    ov <- findOverlaps(query = data_list[[each_dt[1]]], subject = data_list[[each_dt[2]]])
    nnames <<- c(nnames, paste(each_dt, collapse = ':'))
    if(length(ov) == 0){
        return(NULL)
    }

    return(ov)
})

names(ovlaps_list) <- nnames
ovlaps_list
```

# Comment 8
```{verbatim}
How does TFXcan and Enpact compare to other models? 
Can Enpact prioritize known causal variants at GWAS loci better than baseline models (LD score, CADD)? 
Does the model give different variant scores for AR-prostate than AR-breast?
```

```{r}
prca_tfxcan <- data.table::fread("/beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFXcan/data/tfxcan/prostate_cancer_risk.enpactScores.2025-10-21.complete.spredixcan.tsv") %>%
    tidyr::separate_wider_delim(tfbs, delim = '_', names = c('tf', 'tissue', 'chrom', 'start', 'end')) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(locus = paste(chrom, start, end, sep = '_'), start = as.numeric(start), end = as.numeric(end), tf_tissue = paste(tf, tissue, sep = '_')) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(pvalue), !is.na(zscore)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(tf_tissue %in% c('AR_Prostate', 'AR_Breast')) %>%
    dplyr::select(locus, tf, tissue, tf_tissue, chrom, start, end, zscore, pvalue) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!tissue %in% weird_tissues) 
```

```{r}
ar_prostate_breast <- prca_tfxcan %>% 
    dplyr::select(locus, tf_tissue, zscore) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = locus, names_from = 'tf_tissue', values_from = zscore)
```

```{r}
prca_tfxcan %>% 
    dplyr::select(locus, tf_tissue, zscore) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(abs_zscore = abs(zscore)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(tf_tissue) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(
        minimum = min(abs_zscore, na.rm = TRUE),
        Q1 = quantile(abs_zscore, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
        median = median(abs_zscore, na.rm = TRUE),
        Q3 = quantile(abs_zscore, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
        maximum = max(abs_zscore, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean = mean(abs_zscore, na.rm = TRUE),
        standard_deviation = sd(abs_zscore, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>% dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.double), .fns = function(x){round(x, digits = 3)}))
```

```{r}
ctest <- with(ar_prostate_breast, cor.test(AR_Prostate, AR_Breast, method = 'pearson', exact = TRUE))
ctest
```


## Correlation with thresholds


```{r}
fdr_cutoffs <- seq(from = 0.01, to = 1, by = 0.01)

prop_correct_sign <- purrr::map(fdr_cutoffs, function(fdr_cut){
    corr_signif <- dt_enpact_observed_correlations %>% dplyr::mutate(fdr = qvalue::qvalue(spearman_pvalue, fdr.level = fdr_cut)$significant) %>% dplyr::filter(fdr == TRUE) %>% dplyr::pull(spearman_r)
    tb <- table(sign(corr_signif) == 1)
    data.table(fdr_cutoff = fdr_cut, neg_corr = tb[1], pos_corr = tb[2])
}) %>% dplyr::bind_rows() %>% dplyr::mutate(sum_number = neg_corr + pos_corr) %>% tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = !c(fdr_cutoff, sum_number), names_to = 'sign', values_to = 'number')  %>% dplyr::mutate(prop = (number / sum_number))

prop_correct_sign 
```

```{r}
big_plot <- ggplot(prop_correct_sign, aes(x = fdr_cutoff, y = number, fill = sign)) +
    geom_col(col = 'black') +
    scale_fill_manual(name = 'Correlation Sign', values = c('neg_corr' = 'grey', 'pos_corr' = 'darkgreen'), labels = c('-', '+')) + labs(x = 'FDR Cutoff', y = 'Number of Significantly Correlated ARBS', subtitle = 'Enpact vs. Observed:\nNumber of positively or negatively\ncorrelated ARBS at increasing FDR cut-offs') + theme_simple

inset_plot <- big_plot + xlim(0.00, 0.25) + ylim(0, 750) + theme_simple + theme(legend.position = "none") + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.subtitle = element_blank()) + labs(subtitle = NULL)

main_plus_inset <- cowplot::ggdraw() +
  cowplot::draw_plot(big_plot) +
  cowplot::draw_plot(inset_plot, x = 0.1, y = 0.3, width = .3, height = .3)

ggsave(file.path(figures_directory, "comment9.fdr_vs_num_significant.direction.png"), main_plus_inset, width = 5000, height = 4000, dpi = 800, units = 'px')
```

    - Using a known database, define TFs and gene targets,

    - Collect a list of target genes of these TFs. 
        - The gene must appear within 1mb of any of the 140 PrCa loci, and must be in the TF target list.

    - Run a Gene set enrichment analysis.

```{r, eval = F}
# I want to use the program names
program_names <- names(tf_programs)

top.15.programs <- purrr::map(1:(ncol(consensus_programs)-1), function(i){
    cpr <- glue("consensus_contribution_{i}")
    consensus_programs %>% dplyr::select(tf_tissue, all_of(cpr)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(desc(.data[[cpr]])) %>% 
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 15) %>% 
    tidyr::separate_wider_delim(col = tf_tissue, delim = '_', names = c('tf', 'tissue'), cols_remove = F) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(tf) %>% as.data.frame() %>%
    string_db$map(., "tf", removeUnmappedRows = TRUE ) %>% dplyr::mutate(program = program_names[i])
}) %>% dplyr::bind_rows() %>% dplyr::relocate(program)
```

```{r, eval = F}
# for each program, I can calculate the PPI enrichment

# I am also adding the TFs, whose names are not in the interaction networks
enrichment_ppi_results <- purrr::map(program_names, function(nn){

    queryIDs <- unique(top.15.programs %>% dplyr::filter(program == nn) %>% pull(STRING_id))
    ty <- string_db$get_ppi_enrichment(queryIDs)
    ty <- as.data.table(ty)
    colnames(ty) <- c('pvalue', 'interactions', 'expected')
    ty$program <- nn
    return(ty)
}) %>% dplyr::bind_rows() %>% dplyr::relocate(program)
```

```{r, eval = F}
nonInteractors <- list()

# for each program, I can also query the PPI interactions
interactions_ppi_results <- purrr::map(program_names, function(nn){
    queryNAMEs <- unique(top.15.programs %>% dplyr::filter(program == nn) %>% pull(tf))
    queryIDs <- unique(top.15.programs %>% dplyr::filter(program == nn) %>% pull(STRING_id)) 
    
    # get the interactions between these proteins only
    #dt_inter <- string_db$get_interactions(queryIDs)

    # this pull ALL interaction partners 
    qIDs <- queryIDs %>% paste0(collapse = "%0d")
    req <- RCurl::postForm(
        "https://string-db.org/api/tsv/network",
        identifiers = qIDs,
        required_core = "0",
        species     = "9606",
        add_nodes = 0
    )
    ppi <- read.table(text = req, sep = "\t", header = T) %>% dplyr::mutate(program = nn)
    if(nrow(ppi) == 0){
        return(NULL)
    }
    # find which ones don't have partners
    nonPartners <- queryNAMEs[(!queryNAMEs %in% ppi$preferredName_A) & (!queryNAMEs %in% ppi$preferredName_B)]
    if(identical(nonPartners, character(0))){
        nonInteractors[[nn]] <<- NULL 
    } else {
        nonInteractors[[nn]] <<- nonPartners
    }

    return(ppi)
}) %>% Filter(Negate(is.null), .) %>% dplyr::bind_rows() %>% dplyr::relocate(program)


as.data.table(nonInteractors) %>%
    data.table::fwrite(file.path(tfxcan_directory, "experiments/validation/tfxcan_programs.nonInteractors.tsv"), sep = '\t', quote = F, row.names = F, col.names = TRUE)
# save the results so I don't have to do this everytime
interactions_ppi_results %>% 
    data.table::fwrite(file.path(tfxcan_directory, "experiments/validation/tfxcan_programs.interactions.tsv"), sep = '\t', quote = F, row.names = F, col.names = TRUE)
```

```{r}
ppi_graphs <- purrr::map(names(graph_objects), function(pname){
    if(pname %in% c('CTCF', 'REST')){return(NULL)} # remove CTCF; it is just one protein
    pdt <- dt_enrichment %>% dplyr::filter(program == pname)
    nproteins <- igraph::gorder(graph_objects[[pname]])
    pwrite <- ifelse(pdt$pvalue %in% c(0L, 2.22e-16), "p < 2.22e-16", glue("p = {pdt$pvalue}"))

    heading <- glue("{pdt$program}\nTranscription factors: {nproteins}\nInteractions: {pdt$interactions}")

    # heading <- glue("{pdt$program}\nProteins: {nproteins}\nInteractions: {pdt$interactions}\nExpected Interactions: {pdt$expected}\n{pwrite}")

    ggraph(graph_objects[[pname]], layout = 'stress') + 
        geom_edge_link(color = 'white') + 
        geom_node_point(size = 5, color = 'steelblue') +
        geom_node_text(aes(label = name), repel = TRUE) +
        geom_edge_link(aes(width = score), color = 'darkgreen', alpha = 0.5) +
        scale_edge_width(range = c(0.5,1), name="STRING PPI score") +
        labs(title = heading) +
        theme_simple_graph
})
```

```{r}
# calculate probability of the observed value or more
probs_events <- purrr::map(names(null_interactions.list), function(pp){
    dt.null <- null_interactions.list[[pp]]
    if(!is.null(dt.null)){
        obs_n_interactions <- dt_enrichment %>% dplyr::filter(program == pp) %>% dplyr::pull(interactions)
        null_dist <- dt.null$null_n_interactions
        prob_k <- sum(null_dist >= obs_n_interactions) / length(null_dist)
        return(prob_k)
    }
}) 
names(probs_events) <- names(null_interactions.list)
as.data.table(probs_events)
```


```{r}
pp_list <- purrr::map(names(null_interactions.list), function(pp){
    dt.null <- null_interactions.list[[pp]]
    if(!is.null(dt.null)){
        obs_n_interactions <- dt_enrichment %>% dplyr::filter(program == pp) %>% dplyr::pull(interactions)
        p_val <- probs_events[[pp]]
        subt <- glue::glue("Interactions: {obs_n_interactions}\np-value: {p_val}")

        po <- ggplot() +
            geom_histogram(aes(x = dt.null$null_n_interactions, color = 'exp_int'), binwidth = 5) +
            geom_vline(aes(xintercept = obs_n_interactions, color = 'obs_int'), linetype="dashed", linewidth=0.5) + theme_simple +
                labs(x = 'Number of Interactions', y = 'Number of Null Replicates', title = pp, subtitle = subt) +
                scale_color_manual(name = "", values = c(obs_int = "red", exp_int = 'black'), labels = c(obs_int = 'Observed interactions', exp_int = 'Null distribution')) +
            theme( 
                legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),
                legend.box.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = 'transparent'))

                # legend.position.inside = c(0.1, 0.95),
                # legend.position = 'inside',
            return(po)
    } else {
        return(NULL)
    }
})
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
        eresult$program <- grp
        return(eresult)
    }
})


functional_enrichment <- Filter(Negate(is.null), functional_enrichment)

functional_enrichment %>% data.table::fwrite(file.path(tfxcan_directory, "experiments/validation/tfxcan_programs.functional_enrichment.tsv"), sep = '\t', quote = F, row.names = F, col.names = TRUE)
```

```{r}
enrichment_results <- data.table::fread(file.path(tfxcan_directory, "experiments/validation/tfxcan_programs.functional_enrichment.tsv")) %>% dplyr::filter(fdr <= 0.05) %>%
    dplyr::filter(category %in% c("Component", 'Function', 'KEGG', "WikiPathways", "Process", 'RCTM')) %>%

# names(enrichment_splits)

enrichment_plots <- purrr::map(names(enrichment_splits), function(pname){
    ep <- enrichment_results %>%
        dplyr::filter(program == pname, fdr <= 0.05) %>%
        dplyr::arrange(fdr) %>%
        dplyr::select(category, program, description, number_of_genes, fdr, p_value, term, neglogP) %>%
        dplyr::group_by(description) %>% dplyr::slice_min(p_value) %>% ungroup()
        #dplyr::filter(term != 'CL:20715')

    pp <- ggplot(ep, aes(x = neglogP, y = reorder(description, neglogP))) +
        geom_point(aes(size = number_of_genes)) +
        geom_segment(aes(xend=0, yend=description)) +
        theme_simple +
        guides(size = guide_legend(title = 'Gene Count')) +
        labs(x = expression(-log[10]*"P"), y = 'Term', title = unique(pname))

    return(pp)

    #gt <- ggsave(glue("{figures_directory}/enrichment_analysis_on_{pname}.png"), ep, width = 10000, height = 2500, dpi = 800, units = 'px')

    #return(ep)
}, .progress = TRUE)

names(enrichment_plots) <- names(enrichment_splits)
```

# Comment 12

https://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/snp/organisms/human_9606_b151_GRCh38p7/VCF/

```{verbatim}
Do newly identified hits associated with PrCa risk overlap biologically plausible loci and do they replicate in independent GWAS datasets? Or are they mostly correlated with CWAS hits, i.e. they tag the same signal but are labeled distinctly due to resolution?
```

To respond to this comment, I want to know what TFXcan-exclusive ARBS are not likely tagging a CWAS signal. Then I want to know if any of the ARBS have SNPs in them that have been shown to colocalize with prostate cancer molecular qtls. 

First, I can check if these are distinct signals, or if they are correlated with CWAS hits. If the newly-identified sites happen to overlap with CWAS result (using LD), then it is likely that they are being tagged. 

```{r}
# TFXcan and CWAS results. 
dt_recap <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(tfxcan_directory, 'results/files/enpact-paper.supplementary_tables.xlsx'), sheet = 'Supplementary Table 10', skip = 1) %>% 
    tidyr::separate_wider_delim(arbs, delim = '_', names = c('chrom', 'start', 'end'), cols_remove = F) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(start = as.numeric(start), end = as.numeric(end))

#ld information
ldblocks <- data.table::fread(file.path(tfxcan_directory, 'metadata/hg38_fourier_ls-all.bed'), header=F, col.names=c('chrom', 'start', 'end'))
```

```{r}
tfxcan_exclusive <- dt_recap %>% dplyr::filter(is.na(CWAS.Z), !is.na(TFXcan.Z))
cwas_exclusive <- dt_recap %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(CWAS.Z), is.na(TFXcan.Z))

# this is not exactly exclusive. it is the total number of cwas significant ARBS i.e 74
cwas_all <- dt_recap %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(CWAS.Z))
tfxcan_all <- dt_recap %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(TFXcan.Z))

dim(tfxcan_exclusive)
```

How are these split into LD regions?
```{r}
# convert to granges for fast queries and manipulation
ldgranges <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(seqnames = ldblocks$chrom, IRanges::IRanges(start = ldblocks$start, end = ldblocks$end))
results_granges <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(seqnames = dt_recap$chrom, IRanges::IRanges(start = dt_recap$start, end = dt_recap$end))

results_overlaps <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(query = results_granges, subject = ldgranges)
# arbs within ldblock 
arbs_within_ldblocks <- dplyr::bind_cols(
    ldblocks[subjectHits(results_overlaps), ] %>% tidyr::unite('ldblock', chrom:end, sep='_'), dt_recap[queryHits(results_overlaps), ]
)
# some could not be assigned to an LD region
arbs_without_ldblocks <- dt_recap %>% dplyr::filter(!arbs %in% arbs_within_ldblocks$arbs)
arbs_without_ldblocks$ldblock <- NA
arbs_without_ldblocks <- arbs_without_ldblocks %>% dplyr::relocate(ldblock)

arbs_within_ldblocks <- dplyr::bind_rows(arbs_within_ldblocks, arbs_without_ldblocks)
dim(arbs_within_ldblocks)
```

```{r}
dt_complete_arbs <- arbs_within_ldblocks %>% dplyr::mutate(
    signal = dplyr::case_when(
        !is.na(TFXcan.P) & !is.na(CWAS.P) ~ "all",
        is.na(TFXcan.P) & !is.na(CWAS.P) ~ 'CWAS_only',
```

There are 164 ARBS discovered by TFXcan. xx overlap with CWAS results. Of the 118 non-overlapping, TFXcan-exclusive ARBS, 44 are not in LD blocks with any of the CWAS-found ARBS (so, they are less likely to be tagging the CWAS ARBS). The 44 ARBS are organized into 33 LD blocks. So, some of these signals may be tagging each other.

# Comment 17

```{verbatim}
Figure S2A: the Enpact scores seem rather discrete/categorical and many data points have actually the same value between 0 and 1, what does this mean? Consider representing the data in a different way, also to avoid misleading conclusions. The p-value that is shown is obtained by performing a t-test between the two categories even though they are clearly not normally distributed. It would be more informative and accurate to report the comparison between bound and unbound by setting a threshold and assessing false positives instead.
```

```{r}
# Install and load the ROCR package if you haven't already
# install.packages("ROCR")
library(ROCR)

# 1. Prepare your data:
# 'predictions' should be a vector of predicted probabilities from your model.
# 'labels' should be a vector of actual class labels (0 or 1, or factors).
# Example data (replace with your actual data):
set.seed(123)
predictions <- runif(100) # Example predicted probabilities
labels <- sample(c(0, 1), 100, replace = TRUE) # Example true labels

# 2. Create a prediction object:
pred <- prediction(predictions, labels)

# 3. Calculate performance metrics, including FPR:
# The 'performance' function allows you to extract various metrics.
# "fpr" stands for False Positive Rate, and "tpr" for True Positive Rate.
perf <- performance(pred, "fpr", "tpr")

# 4. Extract FPR values and corresponding thresholds:
fpr_values <- perf@x.values[[1]] # FPR values
thresholds <- perf@alpha.values[[1]] # Corresponding thresholds

# You can then inspect these values, for example:
head(data.frame(Threshold = thresholds, FPR = fpr_values))

# 5. Plotting (optional, but common for ROC curves):
plot(perf, colorize = TRUE, main = "ROC Curve")
```

# Reviewer 2 Comment 3
```{verbatim}

In addition, it would be helpful to discuss how sensitive the approach is to the choice of predictive model. While Enformer is a powerful backbone, future iterations of this framework could incorporate alternative architectures such as Beluga, Sei, Borzoi, or AlphaGenome. 
I don't think it is necessary at this point to redo the paper benchmarking each of these methods, but perhaps a small scale comparison of the performance of the linear model using predictions from one of the other models, or at least acknowledging this exploration is worth doing in a future study (if outside the scope of this paper). Framing ENPACT as modular and improvable with advances in sequence-to-function modeling would help contextualize its strengths and future potential.


```

### A database of TF-gene targets

```{r}
tf_gene_targets <- list()
```
```{r}
tf_targets_matrix <- data.table::fread('/beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/Enpact/files/gene_attribute_matrix.txt.gz')
colnames(tf_targets_matrix) <- sapply(strsplit(colnames(tf_targets_matrix), '-'), getElement, 1)
tf_targets_matrix <- tf_targets_matrix %>% tibble::column_to_rownames('Gene') %>% as.matrix()
tf_targets <- lapply(unique(colnames(tf_targets_matrix)), function(x) {
    mx <- tf_targets_matrix[, colnames(tf_targets_matrix) %in% x, drop = FALSE]
    true_targets <- mx[rowSums(mx) > 0, ,drop = F]
    data.table(tf = x, target = rownames(true_targets))
}) %>% do.call(rbind, .)

tf_targets[1:5, ]

tf_gene_targets[['chea']] <- tf_targets
```


### Convert the 140 PrCa loci to a granges object for easy computation

Also expand the PrCa loci to 1mb.
```{r}
prca_loci <- data.table::fread(file.path(tfxcan_directory, 'data/tenerife/consensus/prca_risk.loci_assignments.1000samples.L2_norm.txt.gz'))
prca_loci.granges <- prca_loci %>% 
    dplyr::select(locus) %>% 
    tidyr::separate_wider_delim(col = locus, names = c('chrom', 'start'), delim = ':') %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(end = start) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(c(start, end), as.numeric)) %>% 
    with(., GenomicRanges::GRanges(seqnames = chrom, IRanges::IRanges(start = start, end = end))) %>%
    GenomicRanges::resize(fix = 'center', width = 2000000)
```


### Get a list of all protein coding genes and their locations

```{r}
# getting genes using annotation hub
library(AnnotationHub)

## Load the annotation resource.
ah <- AnnotationHub()
## Query for available H.Sapiens EnsDb databases
ahDb <- query(ah, pattern = c("Homo Sapiens", "EnsDb"))

ensdb <- ah[['AH119325']] # AH119325 | Ensembl 113 EnsDb for Homo sapiens

# filter for chromosomes 1:22
ensdb <- ensembldb::addFilter(ensdb, SeqNameFilter(c(1:22)))
# filter for only protein coding genes
filtr <- GeneBiotypeFilter('protein_coding', condition = "==")
# create genes_Granges
genes_granges <- genes(ensdb, filter = filtr) 
seqlevelsStyle(genes_granges) <- "UCSC"
```


### Find protein-coding genes that are nearby these PrCa genes and that are gene targets of these TFs.
```{r}
genes_loci_overlaps <- findOverlaps(subject = prca_loci.granges, query = genes_granges)
genes_within_1mb <- genes_granges[queryHits(genes_loci_overlaps)]

gene_targets_of_top.15 <- tf_gene_targets[['chea']] %>% dplyr::filter(tf %in% unique(top.15$tf)) %>% dplyr::pull(target)
target_gene_list.granges <- plyranges::filter(genes_within_1mb, gene_name %in% gene_targets_of_top.15)
target_gene_list <- mcols(target_gene_list.granges)$gene_name |> unique()
length(target_gene_list)
```

### Run a gene set enrichment analysis

```{r}
# define a universe; Here, I am using all potential target genes of TFs. 
universe_genes <- tf_gene_targets[['chea']]$target |> unique()
length(universe_genes)
```

```{r,eval = F}
res <- gprofiler2::gost(query = target_gene_list,
                organism = "hsapiens", ordered_query = FALSE,
                multi_query = FALSE, significant = TRUE, exclude_iea = FALSE, 
                measure_underrepresentation = FALSE, evcodes = FALSE, 
                user_threshold = 0.01, correction_method = "fdr", custom_bg = universe_genes, 
                numeric_ns = "", sources = c("GO:MF", "REAC", 'GO:BP', 'GO:CC', 'KEGG'), as_short_link = FALSE, highlight = TRUE)
res$result[1:5, 1:5]; dim(res$result)
```

## Hypothesis 2: The promoters of these target genes are more enriched in motifs of these TFs than other TF' motifs.

### Get a list of the promoters of protein coding genes and their locations

```{r}
# getting genes using annotation hub
library(AnnotationHub)

## Load the annotation resource.
ah <- AnnotationHub()
## Query for available H.Sapiens EnsDb databases
ahDb <- query(ah, pattern = c("Homo Sapiens", "EnsDb"))

ensdb <- ah[['AH119325']] # AH119325 | Ensembl 113 EnsDb for Homo sapiens

# filter for chromosomes 1:22
ensdb <- ensembldb::addFilter(ensdb, SeqNameFilter(c(1:22)))
# filter for only protein coding genes
filtr <- GeneBiotypeFilter('protein_coding', condition = "==")
promoters_granges <- promoters(ensdb, filter = filtr) 
seqlevelsStyle(promoters_granges) <- "UCSC"
```

```{r, eval = F}
# There is no need to run this block except interactively
run_directory <- '/beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFPred-snakemake/data/ENPACT_734_2025-04-24'
dt_train_test <- data.table::fread(file.path(run_directory, 'predictor_files', 'AR_Prostate.predictors.txt'), header = FALSE) # these I trained and tested on 
# I used these in the train-test
# I will expand to 512 bp and turn into Granges to help with overlapping and all that 
granges_train_test <- dt_train_test %>% tidyr::separate_wider_delim(cols = 'V1', delim = '_', names = c('chrom', 'start', 'end'), cols_remove = FALSE) %>% dplyr::mutate(across(c(start, end), as.numeric)) %>% with(GenomicRanges::GRanges(seqnames = chrom, ranges = IRanges(start, end), strand = '*', name = V1))

# the random windows across the genome
granges_50000_windows <- data.table::fread('/beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFXcan/experiments/random_windows/random_50000windows.bed', col.names = c('chrom', 'start', 'end', 'id_num', 'width', 'strand')) %>% with(GenomicRanges::GRanges(seqnames = chrom, ranges = IRanges(start, end), strand = strand))

# to remove windows that overlap here, I will reduce and remove those with width > 512
granges_50000_windows <- GenomicRanges::reduce(granges_50000_windows)
granges_50000_windows <- granges_50000_windows[width(granges_50000_windows) == 513]

valid_chromosomes <- paste0('chr', 1:22)
granges_50000_windows <- GenomeInfoDb::keepSeqlevels(granges_50000_windows, valid_chromosomes, pruning.mode = "coarse")

# find overlaps
ov_granges <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(query = granges_50000_windows, subject = granges_train_test)
length(ov_granges)
```

336 windows in the 50000 random genomic windows set overlap with the training and test set. I will remove these

```{r}

```

Next, I will read in the AR Chip seq and remove 
This is a bit involved. I will be using the training yaml file to get the AR chip seq data
```{r, eval = F}
peaks_folder <- '/project2/haky/Data/TFXcan/cistrome/raw/human_factor'
ar_prostate_peaks_files <- yaml::read_yaml('/beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFPred-snakemake/metadata/enpact_models_to_train_retrain.yaml')[['AR']][['peakFiles']][['Prostate']] %>% file.path(peaks_folder, .)

# I will concatenate all the bed files and sort them
glue::glue("cat {paste(ar_prostate_peaks_files, collapse = ' ')} > /beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFXcan/experiments/random_windows/cistrome_peaks.AR.bed")

# glue::glue("sort -k1,1 -k2,2n /beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFXcan/experiments/random_windows/cistrome_peaks.AR.bed > /beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFXcan/experiments/random_windows/cistrome_peaks.AR.sorted.bed")

# read in, turn to granges and reduce
# reducing will help prevent double counting
granges_ar_peaks_windows <- data.table::fread('/beagle3/haky/users/temi/projects/TFXcan/experiments/random_windows/cistrome_peaks.AR.bed', col.names = c('chrom', 'start', 'end', 'id_num', 'width', 'strand', 'score', 'neglog10p', 'neglog10q', 'value')) %>% with(GenomicRanges::GRanges(seqnames = chrom, ranges = IRanges(start, end), strand = '*')) %>% GenomicRanges::reduce()
valid_chromosomes <- paste0('chr', 1:22)
granges_ar_peaks_windows <- GenomeInfoDb::keepSeqlevels(granges_ar_peaks_windows, valid_chromosomes, pruning.mode = "coarse")

# remove the train-test overlaps
granges_50000_windows_no_train_overlaps <- granges_50000_windows[-S4Vectors::queryHits(ov_granges)] 

# find overlaps
ov_granges <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(query = granges_50000_windows_no_train_overlaps, subject = granges_ar_peaks_windows)
length(ov_granges)
```

Those that overlap are positives. Those that do not, are negatives. 

```{r, eval = F}
pos_granges <- granges_50000_windows_no_train_overlaps[queryHits(ov_granges)] %>% GenomicRanges::reduce()
pos_granges <- pos_granges[width(pos_granges) == 513]
neg_granges <- granges_50000_windows_no_train_overlaps[-queryHits(ov_granges)] %>% GenomicRanges::reduce()
neg_granges <- neg_granges[width(neg_granges) == 513]

length(pos_granges); length(neg_granges)
```

```{r, eval = F}
# select to match the positives
set.seed(2025)

selected_neg_granges <- neg_granges[random_indices]

random_test_windows <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    as.data.table(pos_granges) %>% dplyr::mutate(binding_class = 1),

) %>% dplyr::slice_sample(n = nrow(.)) %>% tidyr::unite('locus', seqnames:end, sep = '_', remove = F)

data.table::fwrite(random_test_windows, file.path(tfxcan_directory, 'experiments/random_windows/test.chip.random_windows.tsv.gz'), sep = '\t', quote = F, col.names = T, row.names = F)
```

## Now that I have the predictions and ground truth, I can analyse the performance and weights.

```{r}
approaches <- c('chip-on-chip', 'chip+motif-on-chip', 'chip+motif-on-chip+motif', 'chip-on-chip+motif')

fullnames <- c('Chip-based AR-Prostate predictors tested on chip-only regions', 'Chip+motif-based AR-Prostate predictors tested on chip-only regions', 'Chip+motif-based AR-Prostate predictors tested on chip+motif regions', 'Chip-based AR-Prostate predictors tested on chip+motif regions')

names(fullnames) <- approaches
fullnames
```

auroc.ci <- calculate_confidence_intervals(feature_sets.predicted_binding[[feau]], 'AR_Prostate', 'binding_class', measure = 'roc', nreplicates = 5000)
    auprc.ci <- calculate_confidence_intervals(feature_sets.predicted_binding[[feau]], 'AR_Prostate', 'binding_class', measure = 'pr', nreplicates = 5000)
    data.frame(
        auprc = calculate_auprc(feature_sets.predicted_binding[[feau]], ycolumn = 'AR_Prostate', labelcolumn = 'binding_class'), 
        auroc = calculate_auroc(feature_sets.predicted_binding[[feau]], ycolumn = 'AR_Prostate', labelcolumn = 'binding_class'), 
        auprc.lower = auprc.ci['2.5%'],
        auprc.upper = auprc.ci['97.5%'],
        auroc.lower = auroc.ci['2.5%'],
        auroc.upper = auroc.ci['97.5%'],
        row.names = feature_sets.full_names[feau]) %>% round(3)

```{r}
list_predictions <- purrr::map(approaches, function(appr){
    xt <- data.table::fread(glue::glue("{tfxcan_directory}/experiments/random_windows/enpact_predicted.AR_Prostate_binding.test.{appr}.random_windows.with_ground_truth.tsv.gz"))
    if("AR_Prostate" %in% colnames(xt)){
        xt <- xt %>% dplyr::rename(AR_Prostate_enpact_score = AR_Prostate )
    }

    return(xt)
})

names(list_predictions) <- approaches
```

```{r}
approaches_performances <- purrr::map(names(list_predictions), function(nt){
    auroc <- calculate_auroc(list_predictions[[nt]], ycolumn = 'AR_Prostate_enpact_score', labelcolumn = "binding_class") %>% round(3)
    auprc <- calculate_auprc(list_predictions[[nt]], ycolumn = 'AR_Prostate_enpact_score', labelcolumn = "binding_class") %>% round(3)
    auprc.ci <- calculate_confidence_intervals(list_predictions[[nt]], 'AR_Prostate_enpact_score', 'binding_class', measure = 'pr', nreplicates = 5000) %>% round(3)
    auroc.ci <- calculate_confidence_intervals(list_predictions[[nt]], 'AR_Prostate_enpact_score', 'binding_class', measure = 'roc', nreplicates = 5000) %>% round(3)

    data.table(method = fullnames[nt], auroc, auroc.lower = auroc.ci['2.5%'], auroc.upper = auroc.ci['97.5%'],
        auprc, auprc.lower = auprc.ci['2.5%'], auprc.upper = auprc.ci['97.5%'])
}) %>% dplyr::bind_rows() %>% dplyr::arrange(desc(auprc))

# write out to use later
approaches_performances %>% data.table::fwrite(file.path(tfxcan_directory, 'experiments/auprc/approaches.peformance.tsv'), sep = '\t', col.names = T, row.names = F, quote = F)
```

```{r, eval = F}
#conversion using rsids
cwas_db_lifted <- cwas_db %>% dplyr::group_by(chr) %>% group_map(.data = ., .f = function(df, key){
    #print(head(df))
    print(key$chr)
    dbsnp_chr <- data.table::fread(glue('https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/snp/organisms/human_9606_b151_GRCh38p7/BED/bed_chr_{key$chr}.bed.gz'), skip = 1, col.names = c('chr', 'start', 'end', 'rsid', 'num', 'strand')) %>% 
        dplyr::filter(rsid %in% df$snp_id) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(hg38_start = start, hg38_end = end) %>%
        dplyr::select(rsid, hg38_start, hg38_end) 
    merged_data <- dplyr::inner_join(df, dbsnp_chr, by = c('snp_id' = 'rsid'))
    return(merged_data)
})
```

```{r}

# cor.test(ddt$num_training_files, ddt$num_1)
```

::: {.callout}
Each point is an Enpact TF-tissue pair. Enpact’s performance is high (AUPRC: range = 0.88 to 0.99; variance = 0.0006) when there are many (greater than 15000, green dashed line) truly bound motifs to learn from. This means that having more truly bound examples improves model performance. However, we find that for several TF-tissue pairs, where the number of truly bound motifs are low in the training data (less than 2000, red dashed line), model performance seems to vary more (AUPRC: range = 0.68 to 1; variance = 0.004) but can still be high. Although having multiple ChIP seq profiling data improves model performance, Enpact’s performance can still be high even when trained on single TF ChIP binding profiles.
:::

```{r}
    if(nrow(out) == 0){
        return(NULL)
    } else {return(out)}
}, .progress = TRUE)

fgt <- Filter(Negate(is.null), fgt)
```
